questions.question: Which method is the usual Java program entry point?
questions.explanation: The JVM starts a standard application at public static void main.

questions.question: Which keyword creates an object?
questions.explanation: The new keyword creates an object.

questions.question: Which collection does not allow duplicate elements?
questions.explanation: HashSet stores unique elements.

questions.question: How many bits does the Java primitive type int occupy?
questions.explanation: An int is always a 32-bit signed two's-complement integer in Java.

questions.question: What is the default value of an uninitialized boolean instance field?
questions.explanation: Instance fields of type boolean default to false.

questions.question: Which modifier on a class prevents it from being subclassed?
questions.explanation: A final class cannot be extended.

questions.question: What does System.out.println(10 / 4); print?
questions.explanation: Both operands are int, so integer division truncates 2.5 to 2.

questions.question: Which access modifier restricts a member to its own class only?
questions.explanation: private members are accessible only within the declaring class.

questions.question: Which expression correctly compares two String objects s1 and s2 for equal content?
questions.explanation: equals compares character content; == compares references.
Strings are immutable; concat returns a new String that is discarded here.

questions.question: Which of these is a checked exception?
questions.explanation: IOException extends Exception but not RuntimeException, so it must be caught or declared.

questions.question: In Java 17, an interface method declared with no body and no modifiers is implicitly:
questions.explanation: Interface methods without a body are implicitly public and abstract.

questions.question: Which call is resolved at runtime based on the actual object type?
options: A call to a static method
A call to a private method
A call to an overridden instance method
questions.explanation: Overridden instance methods use dynamic dispatch; overloading, static and private calls are bound at compile time.

questions.question: Regarding nulls, what does java.util.HashMap allow?
options: One null key and multiple null values
Null keys only, no null values
questions.explanation: HashMap permits a single null key and any number of null values.
Valid indices are 0..2; index 3 fails the runtime bounds check.

questions.question: What does declaring a field static mean?
options: One copy of the field is shared by all instances of the class
Each object gets its own copy
It can only be accessed by static methods of other classes
questions.explanation: A static field belongs to the class itself rather than to individual objects.
Autoboxing caches Integer values from -128 to 127 by default, so only a and b share one object.

questions.question: Which statement about a Java 17 record is true?
options: Its component fields can be reassigned through setters generated automatically
Its component fields are private and final, and the record class is implicitly final
You must write accessor methods yourself
questions.explanation: Records generate private final fields and accessors, implicitly extend java.lang.Record and are final.
A return in finally overrides the return value from the try block.

questions.question: Given sealed interface Shape permits Circle, Square, what must Circle and Square be declared as?
questions.explanation: Every permitted subtype of a sealed type must itself be final, sealed or non-sealed.

questions.question: What does declaring a field volatile guarantee?
options: Only one thread can access it at a time
Writes to it are visible to other threads that read it
questions.explanation: volatile provides visibility and ordering guarantees but not atomicity of compound operations.

questions.question:
What does this print?
System.out.println(new ArrayList<String>().getClass() == new ArrayList<Integer>().getClass());
questions.explanation: Because of type erasure both objects have the same runtime class, ArrayList.
